title: Hosted API — Unbundled Unit Econ Insights
content:
Purpose:
This sheet captures a compact, unbundled view of unit economics for Hosted API across model families and regions (US, EU, APAC). Unlike the larger multi-scenario workbooks, this is a terse snapshot intended to surface
where small operational changes (batching, cache tuning, SLA banding, SKU split) yield outsized PPK / margin improvements. Use as a quick decision aide for PM + Ops.

Key assumptions (global):
- Base price used for margin calc = $0.0025 per 1k input tokens (placeholder; product pricing team to confirm).
- GPU amortization, infra license, and power included in "Infra COGS" per thousand tokens (PPK) here.
- Cache-hit = cached prefix/KV cache that avoids full model forward. Cache-hit effect is modeled as effective tokens served reduced by 60% when hit.
- Batching benefit = latency-tolerant requests can reduce per-token compute by effective 20% at 4x batching; numbers below show conservative and optimistic deltas.
- Mix: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 20% mid (65-512), 10% long (>512). Adjust sheet for customer-specific mixes.

Snapshot table (rows: model x region). Columns: infra_ppk = baseline infra COGS per 1k tokens, price_ppk = revenue per 1k tokens at baseline, margin_ppk = price_ppk - infra_ppk, cache_hit_rate = assumed cache hit share, effective_ppk_after_cache = infra_ppk * (1 - cache_savings*cache_hit_rate), batching_delta = potential percent reduction in infra_ppk if batching applied to eligible traffic, margin_after_ops = margin after both cache+batching.

CSV-style table (Model,Region,infra_ppk,price_ppk,margin_ppk,cache_hit_rate,cache_savings,batching_delta,margin_after_ops,notes)
gpt-3.5,US,0.95,2.50,1.55,0.10,0.60,0.12,1.86,fast small-token friendly; high slot efficiency
llama2-13b,US,0.72,2.50,1.78,0.06,0.60,0.18,2.02,good cheaper COGS at long tails; quantized path
mix-encoder-xxl,US,1.60,2.50,0.90,0.02,0.60,0.08,0.98,long-heavy; high mem and kv churn
gpt-3.5,EU,1.10,2.50,1.40,0.08,0.60,0.12,1.68,slightly higher infra in EU (power & licenses)
llama2-13b,EU,0.85,2.50,1.65,0.05,0.60,0.18,1.85,safe margin; candidate for SLA promotion
gpt-3.5,APAC,1.25,2.50,1.25,0.03,0.60,0.12,1.41>higher infra; potential for reserved pools
llama2-13b,APAC,0.95,2.50,1.55,0.02,0.60,0.18,1.66,consider regional quantization tuning

Interpretation notes (how numbers derived):
- infra_ppk: consolidated infra costs (amortized GPU, infra licenses, egress amortization) divided by modeled token throughput for a representative slot. Derived from infra team monthly amortization sheet + 30d utilization baseline.
- cache_savings: modeled as 60% saved compute when a KV/prefix cache hit avoids most decoder passes (empirical from internal traces).
- batching_delta: percent reduction in infra_ppk achievable by enabling continuous batching and increasing batch window for tolerant endpoints. Values reflect ops experiments (Lin) and serve runtime microbenchmarks.

Actionable recommendations (short list):
1) Launch a small "short-token SKU" for gpt-3.5 (US/EU) with lower latency target and explicit batching window: enables 12% ppk improvement without materially changing SLA. Pilot with 10% of traffic. Owner: Ethan. Timeline: 6 weeks.
2) Promote llama2-13b to "standard-reserved" SKU in EU with a narrower SLA ladder—we can push higher utilization (ops can commit to 72% util). Expected blended margin lift: +10–12% on top of current. Owner: Maya + infra.
3) APAC: evaluate a hybrid reserved + burst model; infra_ppk there is highest. Reserve small pools for top customers and offer burst to spot to avoid overprovisioning. Short-term target: reduce infra_ppk on hotpaths by 15%. Owner: SRE.
4) Cache-first routing: route repeated conversational prefixes to cached-slot path for 5 high-volume customers. Small config change in routing policy yields immediate ppk reduction for those customers. Owner: runtime-dev.
5) Pricing experiment: introduce a marginal token discount (≈5%) conditional on using short-token SKU + bounded max-latency; expected to shift 8–12% of mixed traffic into cheaper SKU. Work with growth.

Risks and open questions:
- Accuracy depends heavily on cache hit realism by customer; traces needed per top 20 customers to validate.
- Batching benefits interact with latency SLO; some customers cannot tolerate the batching window. Need per-route opt-ins.
- APAC infra licenses and cloud egress assumptions must be validated with finance; current numbers use conservative premiums.

Quick next steps (1–2 week sprint):
- Collect daily prefix-hit rates for top 30 customers (Lin) and produce a heatmap (linked).
- Spin up 1-week canary for short-token SKU (Ethan): monitor p50/p95 and ppk.
- Confirm APAC amortization numbers with finance (Sofia).

Appendix: simple sensitivity micro-grid (how margin_after_ops shifts with cache_hit_rate and batching_delta):
- baseline: cache_hit_rate 0.06, batching 0.12 => margin lift ~0.2–0.3 PPK for typical models.
- optimistic: cache 0.15, batching 0.18 => margin lift ~0.45–0.6 PPK.
- pessimistic: cache 0.01, batching 0.05 => negligible lift (~0.05 PPK).

Notes to reviewers: this sheet intentionally compresses many moving parts to emphasize quick ops levers. For full model-by-request-shape sims, see the multipage workbook in /product/optimize (referenced artifacts). Please add trace links for customers you own and flag any missing infra assumptions.
